ranked.name: Katuš shortfall — unrecorded plant/fungal extinction
ranked.source: Kew, State of the World's Plants and Fungi 2026
ranked.known_fact: 29,748 plant species and 411 fungal species assessed as threatened; only 18% of plants and 0.6% of fungi have been assessed; >100,000 plant species and >2 million fungal species remain unnamed; 4,600 plants and 7,800 fungi newly named in 2024–2025; ghost palm Plectocomiopsis hantu named 92 years after first collection. Kew names this the Katuš shortfall: unrecorded loss of known AND unknown species.
ranked.gap_statement: An unnamed plant or fungus can go extinct without minting a death certificate. Red List cannot list what has no name. The loss is real; the record is structurally impossible.
ranked.notes: TODAY'S LOCK. Kew named the biodiversity instance. Class is the cross-realm remainder.
